mainEntity.name: How much water should I store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDC says to store at least 1 gallon of water per person per day for 3 days, and to try for a 2-week supply if possible. Ready.gov says at least one gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation.

mainEntity.name: How long can stored water last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The official guidance gives a rotation cycle, not a shelf life. The CDC says to replace water in containers you filled yourself every six months and to observe the expiration date on store-bought water. Ready.gov says water that has not been commercially bottled should be replaced every six months. Neither page gives a longer period.

mainEntity.name: What is the safest water to store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDC calls unopened, commercially bottled water the safest and most reliable source of water in an emergency. Ready.gov says to keep it in the sealed original container in a cool, dark place.

mainEntity.name: What containers can I use to store water?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDC says it is best to use FDA-approved food-grade water storage containers. If you cannot, choose a container with a tightly closing top, made of durable, unbreakable material (not glass), with a narrow neck or opening if possible. Do not use containers that previously held toxic chemicals such as bleach or pesticides.

mainEntity.name: How do I clean a container before storing water?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDC says to wash it with soap and rinse completely, sanitize it with 1 teaspoon of unscented liquid household chlorine bleach (5% to 9% sodium hypochlorite) in 1 quart (4 cups) of water, cover and shake, wait at least 30 seconds, pour the solution out and let the container dry before filling.

mainEntity.name: Where should I keep stored water?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CDC says to keep containers in a cool place, 50°F to 70°F, away from direct sunlight and away from toxic substances such as gasoline or pesticides. Label each container "drinking water" with the storage date.
